answer: The confirmed global COVID-19 death toll is approximately 7.1 million deaths as of mid-July 2026. However, this is widely recognized as an undercount; the true toll is considerably higher when accounting for incomplete reporting, testing gaps, and excess mortality not officially attributed to COVID-19.
sources: WebSearch 'total global COVID-19 death toll 2026' - ~7.1M confirmed as of mid-July 2026; confirmed count understates true toll; WHO stopped requiring daily reporting 2023-08-25
notes: Worldometer and Our World in Data fetches blocked. Could not verify against primary sources.
_source_conflict: Unlike search_only and verified (both of which asserted a specific >8.5M excess figure conflicting with WHO's ~14.9M), verified_flat gave NO excess-mortality number at all - it stated the direction (higher) without a figure, explicitly because the sources were unreachable. Different failure mode: under-specification rather than a wrong number.
